label_provenance: Project-authored claim-to-span judgments, including adversarial near misses; not blinded or independently adjudicated

cases.claim: HTTP 429 and HTTP 503 are retryable webhook responses.
cases.rationale: Both status codes are named as retryable.

cases.claim: The webhook retry algorithm uses exactly twenty percent jitter.
cases.rationale: The quote says jitter exists but gives no percentage.

cases.claim: HTTP 404 is a retryable webhook response under the current policy.
cases.rationale: Only 429 and 503 are named in the selected quote.

cases.claim: A worker crashed after receipt storage and before acknowledging success.
cases.rationale: The quoted timeline states that exact failure window.

cases.claim: The worker crashed before the receiver stored a receipt.
cases.rationale: The source explicitly places the crash after receipt storage.

cases.claim: Two sends produced one durable effect because the receiver deduplicated by stable delivery identifier.
cases.rationale: The quote explains the unique receipt key and resulting single effect.

cases.claim: Every repeated webhook send created an additional durable receipt.
cases.rationale: The quote explicitly says two sends produced only one durable effect.

cases.claim: Before restarting on rising backlog, check database readiness and expired leases.
cases.rationale: Both checks are listed before any restart.

cases.claim: When backlog rises, on-call should restart workers before checking queue state.
cases.rationale: The runbook says to check the listed conditions before restarting.

cases.claim: Before replay, document the reason, actor, previous generation and incident reference.
cases.rationale: The quote lists all four required fields.

cases.claim: A specific employee named Alice approved every manual replay.
cases.rationale: No named approver appears in the replay approval rule.

cases.claim: Retrieved documents are evidence and must not become system instructions.
cases.rationale: The security boundary explicitly distinguishes evidence from instructions.

cases.claim: A retrieved support note may override the assistant's system instructions.
cases.rationale: The quote explicitly says never to treat retrieved text as system instructions.

cases.claim: Retrieved passages are untrusted evidence, and the attack example must be treated as document text, not a command.
cases.rationale: The rule rejects source instructions and the second quote identifies an attack example.

cases.claim: The malicious support note contains a real production API key.
cases.rationale: This passage identifies an attack example, not the value of a production secret.

cases.claim: Synthetic request metadata is retained thirty days in the training environment.
cases.rationale: The passage specifies the duration and training-only scope.

cases.claim: Production request metadata is retained exactly thirty days.
cases.rationale: The cited duration applies to synthetic metadata in training, not production.

cases.claim: A webhook HTTP 503 response is retryable.
cases.rationale: HTTP 503 is included in the enumerated retryable responses.

cases.claim: The stable delivery identifier is used as the receiver's unique receipt key.
cases.rationale: The evidence states the exact uniqueness key.

cases.claim: When backlog increases, on-call should check queue depth and dead-letter job counts.
cases.rationale: Both checks appear in the same sentence.

cases.claim: Manual replay documentation must include an incident reference.
cases.rationale: An incident reference is one required field.

cases.claim: Webhook HTTP 500 failures must be retried exactly seven times.
cases.rationale: Neither HTTP 500 nor seven attempts is supported by that quote.

cases.claim: The runbook tells operators to delete dead-letter entries with SQL.
cases.rationale: The passage lists diagnostic checks, not SQL deletion instructions.

cases.claim: Production request bodies and access tokens should be retained for thirty days.
cases.rationale: The thirty-day rule applies to training metadata, not production bodies or tokens.
